A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that the presence of lymph node metastases in TNM stage 3 colon or rectal carcinoma is associated with a significantly worse survival outcome, and this association is independent of the presence of extramural venous invasion.
the survival of patients with stage III colorectal cancer is significantly influenced by the number and location of involved lymph nodes and the presence of lymphovascular invasion.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of the use of the novel 4D-MRI method to assess the tumor response in a mouse model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the first time in the literature, we have shown a clear survival advantage for patients undergoing a complete mesocolic excision with D3 lymphadenectomy for stage III colon cancer.
the survival impact of lymph node (LNM) metastasis is not the same in TNM stages IIIA and IIIB, and the survival benefit of chemotherapy is not the same for TNM stages IIIa and IIIB.
